plain_english: Therefore, even in the self-created portion of being, which is essentially one's own nature, this clear appearance of dependence is manifested by the Lord alone.
sanskrit_cite:
tena svasṛṣṭe bhāvāṃśe svarūpātmany api sphuṭam /
pāratantryāvabhāso 'yaṃ devenaivāvabhāsyate // [AgMsv_1.665]

plain_english: The self-dependent supreme Lord fashions dependence; no other defining mark is stated for autonomy and dependence than this.
sanskrit_cite:
pāratantryaṃ kalayati svatantraḥ parameśvaraḥ /
svātantrye pāratantrye ca nānyal lakṣaṇam ucyate // [AgMsv_1.666]

plain_english: For what has limited light is inert; therefore, if the limiter posited here is itself clearly something to be limited, a problem arises.
sanskrit_cite:
paricchinnaprakāśo hi jaḍas tenātra yaḥ sthitaḥ /
paricchedaka eṣo 'pi paricchedyo yadi sphuṭam // [AgMsv_1.667]

plain_english: Then, in grasping its form, light does not shine; for an external portion of being does not shine by itself.
sanskrit_cite:
tad asya rūpagrahaṇe na prakāśaḥ prakāśate /
tathā hi bāhyo bhāvāṃśaḥ svayaṃ naiṣa prakāśate // [AgMsv_1.668]

plain_english: Knowledge is of the nature of illuminating objects, yet if it is unmanifest, even its inherent self does not shine by its own nature.
sanskrit_cite:
jñānam arthaprakāśātma tac cānābhātam eva hi /
tasyāpi samavāyy ātmā naiva bhāti svarūpataḥ // [AgMsv_1.669]

plain_english: Its instrument, such as the eye, does not shine by itself; and without consciousness there is no manifestation at all, even with light and other aids.
sanskrit_cite:
tadīyakaraṇaṃ netraprabhṛty api na bhāsate /
ālokādeś ca vijñānād ṛte naivāvābhāsanam // [AgMsv_1.670]

plain_english: But if, when knowledge arises, that luminosity of the object is its own power or property, then omniscience would follow throughout the whole universe.
sanskrit_cite:
nanu jātaṃ yadi jñānam arthasyāsau prakāśatā /
śaktir dharmo yadi prāptaṃ sārvajñyaṃ viśvamaṇḍale // [AgMsv_1.671]

plain_english: Or if that so-called luminosity is taken as something else, it does not fit coherently anywhere among the known, the knower, and the means of knowing.
sanskrit_cite:
anyad evātha tat kiṃcit prakāśatvābhiśabditam /
tan meyamātṛmāneṣu naiva kutrāpi saṃgatam // [AgMsv_1.672]

plain_english: Therefore this whole universe would always remain unmanifest; and if an unmanifest being were to become illuminated, another difficulty follows.
sanskrit_cite:
tataś cāprakaṭaṃ viśvaṃ sarvadaiva bhaved idam /
aprakāśasya bhāvasya yadi ca syād prakāśanam // [AgMsv_1.673]

plain_english: By that much its own nature would be lost; and if the arising of knowledge is the manifestation of a being while it remains in its own nature, that must be explained.
sanskrit_cite:
tāvataivāsya hīyeta svarūpaṃ parihānitaḥ /
jñānotpattiś ca bhāvasya svarūpasthasya cet prathā // [AgMsv_1.674]

plain_english: If a being remains undifferentiated in its own nature, why would that manifestation not belong to the whole universe? Therefore the light of the universe rests in the limiter.
sanskrit_cite:
aviśiṣṭe svarūpasthabhāve viśvasya sā na kim /
tasmāt prakāśo viśvasya paricchedakaniṣṭhitaḥ // [AgMsv_1.675]

plain_english: If the limiter, differentiated by varied forms arising from the manifestation of its own freedom, were itself something to be limited, then a consequence follows.
sanskrit_cite:
tatsvātantryāvabhāsotthacitrākāravibheditaḥ /
paricchedaka itthaṃ cet paricchedyo bhavet tataḥ // [AgMsv_1.676]

plain_english: Then this root-destroying infinite regress would occur; therefore that limiter is said to be unlimited.
sanskrit_cite:
mūlakṣatikarī seyam anavasthā patiṣyati /
ataś ca so 'paricchinnaḥ paricchedaka ucyate // [AgMsv_1.677]

plain_english: Therefore it is not constructible and, as the scriptures say, not within the domain of time; for that reason the condition of being a knowable object is explained as belonging to time.
sanskrit_cite:
akālpyas tena śāstreṣu tan na kālasya gocaraḥ /
tenāsya vedyadharmatvaṃ kālasya paribhāṣitam // [AgMsv_1.678]

plain_english: If time were to delimit the subject, then the stability of time would certainly depend on the subject and would require the subject's functioning.
sanskrit_cite:
yadi kālaś ca mātāraṃ paricchindyāt tato dhruvam /
mātṛlagnaiva kālasya sthitir nirvāham icchati // [AgMsv_1.679]

plain_english: And no other subject could be posited, because of infinite regress; to remove that regress, this subject must be accepted as free from the divisions of time.
sanskrit_cite:
na ca mātrantaraṃ kiṃcit saṃbhaved anavasthiteḥ /
tāṃ hantuṃ vopagamyo 'sau mātā kālakalojjhitaḥ // [AgMsv_1.680]

plain_english: But if the limited subject is indeed dependent on that time, then how, in your view, can one and the same entity be both subject and object?
sanskrit_cite:
ya eva tu paricchedyo mātā tallagna eva cet /
sa kālo mātṛmeyatve tarhy ekasya kathaṃ tava // [AgMsv_1.681]

plain_english: For in the doctrine of difference your view is fixed in that way; but for us, who uphold non-difference, let there be no such refutation at all.
sanskrit_cite:
bhedavāde hi bhavatāṃ niṣṭhitā matir īdṛśī /
abhedavādināṃ nas tu naiva kāpy astu khaṇḍanā // [AgMsv_1.682]

plain_english: For those for whom the universe consists of the subject and the subject likewise consists of the universe, the supreme Lord is not entangled in the mire of the nets of time and limiting factors.
sanskrit_cite:
viśvaṃ mātṛmayaṃ yeṣāṃ mātā viśvamayas tathā /
tan na kālakalājālajambālaiḥ parameśvaraḥ // [AgMsv_1.683]

plain_english: For the light of the power of consciousness takes on a kind of tarnish; therefore it appears concealed at that time and later appears in manifest form.
sanskrit_cite:
citiśaktiprakāśo hi mālinyam avalambate /
atas tadā saṃvṛto 'sau paścāt prakaṭarūpakaḥ // [AgMsv_1.684]

plain_english: Thus this unfolding, which designates that condition, belongs to that same reality alone; it is a certain creative construal of its own, whose nature is reflective awareness of its own form.
sanskrit_cite:
iti tasyaiva jṛmbheyaṃ tathātvavyapadeśinī /
kalanaivāsya sā kācit svarūpāmarśanātmikā // [AgMsv_1.685]

plain_english: In that construal the self regards itself as fit for union with Śiva; for through connection with variety it comes to regard itself in that way.
sanskrit_cite:
śivayogārham ātmānaṃ yasyām ātmābhimanyate /
yato vaicitryayogena tathātmānaṃ sa manyate // [AgMsv_1.686]

plain_english: Therefore the descent of power is taught here as ninefold; otherwise the Lord would have attachment or aversion somewhere, which he does not.
sanskrit_cite:
śaktipātasya tenoktā navadhātra vyavasthitiḥ /
anyathā neśvarasyāsti rāgo dveṣo 'tha vā kvacit // [AgMsv_1.687]

plain_english: For if this all-pervading Lord were to send down his own power in a fixed way anywhere, that would imply a motive; thus this descent of power of the great Lord is without external cause.
sanskrit_cite:
yena kvāpy eṣa niyatāṃ svāṃ śaktiṃ pātayed vibhuḥ /
animittas tathā cāyaṃ śaktipāto maheśituḥ // [AgMsv_1.688]

plain_english: By decay of attachment, equality of karma, weight of good deeds, ripening of impurity, union with a friend, devotion, feeling, and practice.
sanskrit_cite:
tena rāgakṣayāt karmasāmyāt sukṛtagauravāt /
malapākāt suhṛdyogād bhakter bhāvāc ca sevanāt // [AgMsv_1.689]

plain_english: From practice, breaking of latencies, ripening of impressions, decay of false knowledge, renunciation of karma, and falling away of desire.
sanskrit_cite:
abhyāsād vāsanodbhedāt saṃskāraparipākataḥ /
mithyajñānakṣayāt karmasaṃnyāsāt kāmyavicyuteḥ // [AgMsv_1.690]

plain_english: That power descends from equality of mind is said, but that is unreal; even there another cause must be sought.
sanskrit_cite:
sāmyāc cittasya sā śaktiḥ patatīti yad ucyate /
tad asan /
nanu tatrāpi nimittāntaramārgaṇāt // [AgMsv_1.691]

plain_english: From the absence of infinite regress and from avoiding mutual dependence, circularity, and similar faults.
sanskrit_cite:
anavasthātiprasaṅgasaṃbhavābhāvayogataḥ /
anyonyāśrayaniḥśreṇicakrakādyupapātataḥ // [AgMsv_1.692]

plain_english: In this view, even all doctrines have a fitting standing; in the all-enduring view, nothing is indeed faulted.
sanskrit_cite:
asmiṃs tu pakṣe sarveṣāṃ pravādānām api sthitiḥ /
yuktā sarvaṃsahe pakṣe na kiṃcit kila duṣyati // [AgMsv_1.693]

plain_english: Wise ones can join it themselves there; therefore separate joining is not said here, and this textual expansion is false.
sanskrit_cite:
yuktiḥ sudhībhiḥ svayam eva tatra śakyeta saṃyojayitum tato na /
pṛthaktayā yojanam uktam atra yad granthato vistara eṣa mithyā // [AgMsv_1.694]

plain_english: Therefore they approached independent Shiva-power; without her there is no liberation-state, so liberation-talks in other scriptures are in vain.
sanskrit_cite:
upajagmur ato 'napekṣiṇīṃ śivaśaktiṃ na ca tāṃ vinā bhavet /
apavargapadaṃ yato mudhā paraśāstreṣu vimokṣasaṃkathāḥ // [AgMsv_1.695]

plain_english: At the time of power-descent inquiry is proper, Lord, yet you never do it; the venerable Utpala teacher showed such inquiry there in his own scripture.
sanskrit_cite:
śaktipātasamaye vicāraṇaṃ prāptam īśa na karoṣi karhicit /
śrīmadutpalagurur nyarūpayat tatra tatra nijaśāstra īdṛśam // [AgMsv_1.696]

plain_english: By his grace alone devotion is produced in men, by which they go to supreme perfection with mind gone to his state.
sanskrit_cite:
tasyaiva hi prasādena bhaktir utpādyate nṛṇām /
yayā yānti parāṃ siddhiṃ tadbhāvagatamānasaḥ // [AgMsv_1.697]

plain_english: Thus in the puranas and scriptures first, that supreme power is declared independent, for in dependence there is lack of lordship.
sanskrit_cite:
itthaṃ purāṇaśāstrādau śaktiḥ sā pārameśvarī /
nirapekṣaiva kathitā sāpekṣatve hy anīśatā // [AgMsv_1.698]

plain_english: Only by blind views hidden by dualism does difficulty of capacity of this power arise, by rule of its sometimes standing.
sanskrit_cite:
kevalaṃ bhedavādāndhyasthagitālasadṛṣṭibhiḥ /
duḥsamarthatvam etasyā niyamena kvacitsthiteḥ // [AgMsv_1.699]

plain_english: Constantly considering karma, impurity, equality, and ripening in nets of such causes, the vain self is exhausted.
sanskrit_cite:
paryālocyāniśaṃ karmamalasāmyaprapākataḥ /
ityādihetujāleṣu vṛthātmā parikhedyate // [AgMsv_1.700]

plain_english: That is not for their benefit, like clinging to grass; therefore he indeed is endowed with such own autonomy.
sanskrit_cite:
tat teṣāṃ nopakārāya kuśakāśāvalambanam /
tasmāt sa eva tādṛkṣasvasvātantryopabṛṃhitaḥ // [AgMsv_1.701]

plain_english: Then so it appears with such variety; thus all views are right here in the supreme Lord.
sanskrit_cite:
tadā tathā tathetyādivaicitryeṇāvabhāsate /
tad itthaṃ sarvadṛṣṭīṇām atraiva parameśvare // [AgMsv_1.702]

plain_english: Entry thus by others, enough, or with reasoning pomp; that own nature is here declared by the god of gods.
sanskrit_cite:
anupraveśa ity anyair alaṃ vā yuktiḍambaraiḥ /
tad itthaṃ devadevena svasvarūpam ihoditam // [AgMsv_1.703]

plain_english: Direct perception there is its measure, supreme among all measures; some held one such measure thus.
sanskrit_cite:
pratyakṣaṃ tatra tanmānaṃ sarvamānadhuroddhuram /
ekam evedṛśaṃ mānam iti kecit prapedire // [AgMsv_1.704]

plain_english: From smoke fire, thus mostly; this is his manifestation, as of a pot fixed by seeing its first part.
sanskrit_cite:
dhūmād agnir iti prāyas tasyaivaitad vijṛṃbhitam /
yathā ghaṭasya pūrvāṃśadṛṣṭaikapariniṣṭhitaḥ // [AgMsv_1.705]

plain_english: Mother, grasping such form, having considered clear mind indeed, direct perception attains.
sanskrit_cite:
mātā sphuṭāsphuṭākāratāvadarthāvalehinīm /
sphuṭām eva matiṃ matvā pratyakṣatvaṃ prapadyate // [AgMsv_1.706]

plain_english: Not and inference in the final part; awareness is one indeed, because fire is known within smoke perception, so.
sanskrit_cite:
na cānumānam antyāṃśe saṃvid ekaiva sā yataḥ /
dhūmādhyakṣapratītyantarniviṣṭāgniprathā tathā // [AgMsv_1.707]

plain_english: One indeed, so far grasping an object part, mind arises; to that extent in part clear form is direct perception, thus let it be said.
sanskrit_cite:
ekaiva tāvad arthāṃśalehinī jāyate matiḥ /
tāvaty āṃśe sphuṭākārā pratyakṣam iti bhāṣyatām // [AgMsv_1.708]

plain_english: As variety of gems, so from establishment of impressions in eye, mind, light, object, etc., in awareness.
sanskrit_cite:
yathā ratnādivaicityraṃ tathā saṃskārasaṃsthiteḥ /
netrātmamānasālokaviṣayādiṣu saṃvidi // [AgMsv_1.709]

plain_english: Direct perception indeed in awareness appears as clear, so from establishment of such pervasion, light, and impression.
sanskrit_cite:
pratyakṣam eva saṃvittau sphuṭatvenāvabhāsate /
tathā tathāvidhavyāptidhāmasaṃkārasaṃsthiteḥ // [AgMsv_1.710]

plain_english: At the end, so indeed that awareness having smoke-fire form, as firm impressions with clear marks immediately oneself.
sanskrit_cite:
ante tathaiva sā vittir dhūmāgnyākārarūpiṇī /
yathā ca dṛḍhasaṃskārāḥ sollekhāḥ sapadi svayam // [AgMsv_1.711]

plain_english: Gem etc. reality they see, obstructed by inner obstacle; so hungry selves quickly, very certain indeed.
sanskrit_cite:
ratnāditattvaṃ paśyanti vighnāntaratirodhitaḥ /
tathā bubhukṣitātmānaḥ śīghram evātiniścitam // [AgMsv_1.712]

plain_english: People take food to eat without any intervening inference of pervasion or the like; therefore what the opponents call mere conceptual construction is already answered and refuted.
sanskrit_cite:
annādi gṛhṇate bhoktuṃ vyāptyādyavyavadhānataḥ /
tena pratyuktam eva syād yad āhuḥ parikalpanam // [AgMsv_1.713]

plain_english: In matters that have become well practiced, where awareness of invariable pervasion is already present, what use is there for a cognition pervaded by conceptual construction? We do not accept that.
sanskrit_cite:
abhyasteṣv avinābhāvasvabhāvavyāptisaṃvidaḥ /
kiṃ hi tatkalpanāvyāptivitter iti na manmahe // [AgMsv_1.714]

plain_english: Because this cognition arises very quickly, it is not clearly noticed; so the opponent infers that it must be conceptual construction. That is the move being stated here.
sanskrit_cite:
āśūtpattivaśād asyā na khalv asty upalakṣaṇam /
anumīyata evaṃ sā tad eva parikalpanam // [AgMsv_1.715]

plain_english: Alas, these people who fancy themselves logicians, blinded by loyalty to their own side, have begun again and again to forget even what they themselves have accepted.
sanskrit_cite:
aho svapakṣapātāndhāḥ svam apy upagataṃ muhuḥ /
amī vismartum ārabdhās tārkikammanyabuddhayaḥ // [AgMsv_1.716]

plain_english: For in your own view, every cognition lasts only a moment and manifests its object simply by arising.
sanskrit_cite:
kṣaṇāpavargiṇī buddhiḥ sarvaiva hi bhavanmatā /
utpattimātrayogena viṣayasyāvabhāsikā // [AgMsv_1.717]

plain_english: If swift manifestation means nothing more than what happens in a moment, then in truth every cognition would be swiftly manifesting.
sanskrit_cite:
na kṣaṇāc cāparaṃ kiṃcid āśubhāvitvam ucyate /
tat sarvam āśubhāvy eva vijñānam iti tattvataḥ // [AgMsv_1.718]

plain_english: Then non-noticing would occur everywhere among all things; or else, in the case of unbroken seeing, what is known would have to range over a longer time.
sanskrit_cite:
sarvatra bhāvajāteṣu bhaved anupalakṣaṇam /
athāvicchinnadṛṣṭīnāṃ drāghīyaḥkālagocaram // [AgMsv_1.719]

plain_english: Then even on that view the object is manifested by mere arising; and if clarity of the object is also due simply to arising, that same fact must explain everything.
sanskrit_cite:
jñātaṃ tenāpi tarhy artho janmamātreṇa bhāsyate /
yac cotpattivaśād eva viṣayasphuṭatātmakam // [AgMsv_1.720]

plain_english: How can the fact that the experience is quicker make a difference, if that cognition is said to be self-luminous, even while being related to grasping?
sanskrit_cite:
tasya śīghratarasthāsnubhāvo bhedāvahaḥ katham /
yat tat kila grahāpekṣaṃ svaprakāśam athāpi sat // [AgMsv_1.721]

plain_english: If it becomes a means elsewhere, like lightning or a lamp, then the difference between lasting long or briefly may appear right there as a basis for difference.
sanskrit_cite:
anyatropāyatāṃ yāti vidyuddīpādivat tathā /
tatraiva ciraśīghrasthabhāvo bhedāya bhāsate // [AgMsv_1.722]

plain_english: And in inferences the grasping of pervasion and so on does not become clear again and again in such a way that it would be separately noticed.
sanskrit_cite:
na ca kvāpy anumāneṣu vyāptyāder grahaṇaṃ bhavet /
punaḥ punaḥ sphuṭībhāvaṃ yāti yenopalakṣyate // [AgMsv_1.723]

plain_english: Moreover, even if a clear series of successive cognitions of smoke and so on arises, how could that produce the manifestation of a single thing?
sanskrit_cite:
kiṃ ca kramikadhūmādijñānamālātmani sphuṭam /
uditāpi kathaṃ kuryād ekabhāvāvabhāsanam // [AgMsv_1.724]

plain_english: If one says the final connecting cognition will do this, that too is distinct and just like the earlier cognitions—so how could it unify them in that way?
sanskrit_cite:
athāntyam anusandhānajñānam evaṃ kariṣyati /
tad api prāksthasaṃvittisamaṃ bhinnaṃ kathaṃ tathā // [AgMsv_1.725]

plain_english: If that final cognition is supposed to connect the earlier series of cognitions, but those earlier cognitions no longer exist, then no connection is possible once they have perished.
sanskrit_cite:
tena prāktanavijñānamālāmanvasyate yadi /
tad asan na hi saṃdhānaṃ naṣṭāyām upapadyate // [AgMsv_1.726]

plain_english: If one says that memory itself is the connection between cognitions, how could that memory arise at all in the absence of experience?
sanskrit_cite:
atha smaraṇam eveha saṃdhānaṃ saṃvidāṃ bhavet /
tad apy anubhavābhāve kathaṃ nāma bhaviṣyati // [AgMsv_1.727]

plain_english: And in your view there is no pair of cognitions existing simultaneously; so an experience of cognitions by awareness does not fit anywhere in that system.
sanskrit_cite:
na ca jñāneṣv anubhavo yujyate saṃvidaḥ kvacit /
yugapaj jñānayugalaṃ nāstīti hi bhavanmatam // [AgMsv_1.728]

plain_english: The relation of cognition and its object is observed only where two factors stand together at the same time, not where they arise successively as earlier and later and are therefore opposed.
sanskrit_cite:
jñānajñeyātmatā dṛṣṭā yugapatsthitatājuṣoḥ /
na tu pūrvāparākārasamutpannavirodhinoḥ // [AgMsv_1.729]

plain_english: Therefore, even the cognition that seems to be preceded by a manifestation following pervasion is, in that very case, a non-sequential knowing of a directly perceptual kind.
sanskrit_cite:
tasmād vyāptyanusārāvabhāsapūrvāpi yā matiḥ /
tatrāpy akramam evedaṃ pratyakṣamānavedanam // [AgMsv_1.730]

plain_english: Just as someone suddenly awakened from deep sleep, with eyes just opening, acts to remove the dimness in the appearance of things, taking them directly...
sanskrit_cite:
yathā jhaṭiti sauṣuptaprabuddhaḥ pronmiṣaddṛṣiḥ /
pratyakṣam iti bhāvāṃśadhyāmalatvanivṛtaye // [AgMsv_1.731]

plain_english: While rubbing the eyes and so on, that person does not think, 'I am inferring these things.' Let the same be understood in this case as well.
sanskrit_cite:
netrasaṃmārjanādīni vidadhannābhimanyate /
bhāvān anuminomīti tathaivātrāpi buddhyatām // [AgMsv_1.732]

plain_english: And just as someone whose vision has just emerged from the delusion of deep sleep may, for that moment, forget himself and the place he is in...
sanskrit_cite:
yathā ca ghanasauṣuptamohāvyutthitadarśanaḥ /
svātmānam atha tatsthānaṃ vismaraty eva tat kṣaṇaṃ // [AgMsv_1.733]

plain_english: Then, when his own clear seeing is awakened through gathered effort, he recognizes, 'I am that one,' and in the ultimate sense this comes from awareness itself.
sanskrit_cite:
atha prayatnasaṃbhāraprabuddhavimalasvadṛk /
so 'ham asmīti manvānaḥ saṃvitteḥ paramārthataḥ // [AgMsv_1.734]

plain_english: In all of this, the Lord Bhairava, whose very nature is consciousness, freely conceals and reveals his own form.
sanskrit_cite:
tatra sarvatra nātho 'yaṃ bhairavaś citsvarūpakaḥ /
svātantryāt svaṃ vapur yāvad gūhate vivṛṇoti ca // [AgMsv_1.735]

plain_english: To that extent ignorance arises, and knowledge arises; and that knowledge, by its clarity, should be understood as directly evident to all.
sanskrit_cite:
tāvad ajñānam etasya vijñānaṃ copajāyate /
tac ca sphuṭatayā sarvapratyakṣam iti manyatām // [AgMsv_1.736]

plain_english: When the word 'pot' is heard, a cognition arises of its broad base, belly, and other features; in that cognition, convention, memory, and similar factors are present in the same way.
sanskrit_cite:
ghaṭaśabde śrute yā ca pṛthubudhnodarādidhīḥ /
tatrāpi khalu samketasmaraṇādi tathāvidham // [AgMsv_1.737]

plain_english: Just as in examining a gem one awakens one's own clear awareness through assemblages of other cognitions, so that awareness stands forth distinctly.
sanskrit_cite:
yathā ratnaparīkṣāyāṃ svāṃ saṃvittiṃ sphuṭātmikām /
samvidantarasaṃghātais tiṣṭhati pratibodhayan // [AgMsv_1.738]

plain_english: Then, through the connection with the final awakened clear awareness, the reality of the gem shines forth; at that point the other cognitions have no further use.
sanskrit_cite:
tataḥ prabuddhacaramasphuṭasaṃvittiyogataḥ /
ratnatattvaṃ vibhāty atra nopayoge 'nyasaṃvidām // [AgMsv_1.739]

plain_english: Those other cognitions exercised causality only for awakening that awareness; for in the very connection of its manifestation, they have no usefulness.
sanskrit_cite:
tāḥ paraṃ tatprabodhāya kāraṇatvaṃ vitenire /
tasyaivāvabhāsayoge hi na tāsām upayogitā // [AgMsv_1.740]

plain_english: From such an example as the knowledge of a child and a gem-cutter, in verbal cognition too there is indeed by itself one clear cognition of illumination.
sanskrit_cite:
bālavaikaṭikajñānadṛṣṭāntād īdṛśāt svayam /
śābde 'pi khalu vijñāne sphuṭaivaikā prakāśadhīḥ // [AgMsv_1.741]

plain_english: Therefore, when such a word is heard, whatever cognition arises immediately after in the manifestation of meaning, that cognition is of this extent and of such a character.
sanskrit_cite:
atas tathāvidhe śabde śrute yat samanantaram /
arthāvabhāsane seyam iyatī matir īdṛśī // [AgMsv_1.742]

plain_english: That meaning, of that extent, stands there like the prior and posterior parts of a pot. But surely that pot may be one whole composed of parts?
sanskrit_cite:
arthaḥ sa tāvāṃs tatrāste ghaṭapūrvāparāṃśavat /
nanv asau ghaṭa ekaḥ syād avayavyātmakas tathā // [AgMsv_1.743]

plain_english: But there is no unity of word and meaning, so how could there be such sameness? Alas, one whose eyes are clouded by the darkness of habitual grasping of difference!
sanskrit_cite:
na tu śabdārthayor aikyaṃ tat kathaṃ sāmyam īdṛśam /
aho bhedagrahābhyāsatimirāvilalocanaḥ // [AgMsv_1.744]

plain_english: Even with the application of the collyrium of true reasoning, he has not attained clear vision. This undivided Lord Bhairava assumes within himself the state of both the enjoyed and the enjoyer.
sanskrit_cite:
sadyuktyañjanayoge 'pi na dṛṣṭiṃ vimalāṃ gataḥ /
abhinno bhagavān eṣa bhairavo bhogyabhoktṛtām // [AgMsv_1.745]

plain_english: Having unified everything within himself, always full-bodied — when this has been established previously, what possibility remains for this question?
sanskrit_cite:
ātmany evānusandhāya sarvadā pūrṇavigrahaḥ /
iti prasādhite pūrvaṃ kaḥ praśnasyāsya saṃbhavaḥ // [AgMsv_1.746]

plain_english: Therefore, thus, in comparison and in other means of knowing as well, it is clearly the form of awareness-perception alone that appears everywhere.
sanskrit_cite:
tad evam upamānādāv api mānāntare sphuṭam /
saṃvitpratyakṣarūpaiva sarvatra pratibhāsate // [AgMsv_1.747]

plain_english: Even a blind person, perceiving each respective form through touch, sound, and so on, cognizes that clarity of just such a kind.
sanskrit_cite:
andho 'pi sparśaśabdādyais tattadrūpaṃ vilokayan /
sphuṭatām eva tāṃ tāvat saṃvetti sa tathāvidhām // [AgMsv_1.748]

plain_english: Thus those congenitally deaf apprehend an aspect of things clearly through form, touch, and so on; for them cognition is never unknown anywhere.
sanskrit_cite:
evaṃ jātijaḍā rūpasparśādyair abhimanvate /
sphuṭam eva hi bhāvāṃśaṃ teṣāṃ nājñātadhīḥ kvacit // [AgMsv_1.749]

plain_english: Saying 'this is a lake of beauty, a shoot in the garden of youth,' a congenitally blind person is pleased from touching her limbs.
sanskrit_cite:
iyaṃ lāvaṇyasarasī tāruṇyodyānakaṇḍalī /
iti tuṣyati jātyandhas tadaṅgaparimarśanāt // [AgMsv_1.750]

plain_english: Saying 'ah, he sings with ornament,' a deaf person, merely by seeing the singer's face, is satisfied by that alone.
sanskrit_cite:
aho nu sadalaṃkāraṃ gāyatīti jaḍo janaḥ /
gātur mukhaṃ vilokyaiva tāvatā parituṣyati // [AgMsv_1.751]

plain_english: Thus perception alone expands without rival; therefore a brief consideration of its fruit and so on is now begun.
sanskrit_cite:
iti pratyakṣam evaikaṃ niḥsapatnaṃ vijṛmbhate /
tad asya phalacintādi kartuṃ prastūyate manāk // [AgMsv_1.752]

plain_english: That very cognition is surely of the nature of the essence of reflective awareness; therefore talk of difference is not at all well suited with regard to its fruit.
sanskrit_cite:
tad eva khalu vijñānaṃ parimarśarasātmakam /
tasmād bhedakathā naiva phalaṃ prati susaṃgatā // [AgMsv_1.753]

plain_english: Let avoidance and similar cognitions be the fruit; yet even that comes from manifestation. Or else, awareness is self-luminous and ultimate.
sanskrit_cite:
hānādidhīḥ phalaṃ vāstu tasyā apy atha bhāsanāt /
yadi vā svaprakāśaiva saṃvittiḥ pāramārthikī // [AgMsv_1.754]

plain_english: That indeed is the final fruit, well determined everywhere; joy and so on, which is spoken of everywhere here as the primary fruit, is included in it.
sanskrit_cite:
tad eva paryanthaphalaṃ sarvatraiva suniścitam /
hlādādikaṃ phalaṃ mukhyaṃ yat sarvatreha gīyate // [AgMsv_1.755]

plain_english: It comes to rest in that own awareness, in the full self. Therefore, thus, this perception fully expands on all sides.
sanskrit_cite:
tatsvasaṃvidi viśrāntim abhyeti bharitātmani /
tad evam idam adhyakṣaṃ sarvataḥ pravijṛmbhate // [AgMsv_1.756]

plain_english: For one devoted to the practice of this, what accomplishment does not arise? Beginning from kala and so on, through an inclination toward hearing what is spoken by Brahma and others...
sanskrit_cite:
etadabhyāsaniṣṭḥasya keva siddhir na jāyate /
brahmādibhāṣitaśrautapraunmukhyena kalādikāt // [AgMsv_1.757]

plain_english: Hearing-cognition from afar quickly arises; even in an aspect of a thing seen by the mind, the arising of clear cognition indeed occurs abundantly.
sanskrit_cite:
dūrāc chravaṇavijñānam acirāt saṃpravartate /
manodṛṣṭe 'pi bhāvāṃśe sphuṭavṛttyudayo hy alam // [AgMsv_1.758]

plain_english: What wonder is it if this arises when overcome by the power of one's own reflective awareness? So it is said in the Spanda scripture, even in an attentive mind.
sanskrit_cite:
svavimarśabalākrānte kiṃ citraṃ yadi jāyate /
spandaśāstre tathā coktaṃ sāvadhāne 'pi cetasi // [AgMsv_1.759]

plain_english: It shines forth ever more clearly — enough of much elaboration. In this way, this entire universe is indeed the perception of the supreme lord.
sanskrit_cite:
bhūyaḥ sphuṭataro bhātīty alaṃ bahulavistaraiḥ /
itthaṃ pratyakṣam evedaṃ viśvaṃ yat parameśituḥ // [AgMsv_1.760]

plain_english: Even though the group of knowing subjects is undivided, there is no confusion of cognitions, because each cognition arises through its own distinct mode of manifestation.
sanskrit_cite:
tat tato 'py avibhinnasya mātṛvargasya tat tathā /
na ca pratītisāṃkāryaṃ tathā bhāsanayogataḥ // [AgMsv_1.761]

plain_english: Even when perception operates in the same field, the cognition of a pot and of a non-pot are not identical; thus perception itself shines forth unrivaled.
sanskrit_cite:
pratyakṣe 'pi same sāmyaṃ no ghaṭāghaṭasamvidoḥ /
itthaṃ pratyakṣam evedaṃ niḥsapatnaṃ vijṛmbhate // [AgMsv_1.762]

plain_english: For that reason the object is not divided, and such nonduality of perception is recognized by one whose understanding is firmly established in the unifying insight.
sanskrit_cite:
tato na bhidyate cārthaḥ pratyakṣādvaitam īdṛśam /
idaṃ sandhānakalikāpariniṣṭhitabuddhinā // [AgMsv_1.763]

plain_english: Teacher Narasiṃha teaches the nonduality of perception, while some others claim that inference is the valid means of knowing for the entire universe.
sanskrit_cite:
ācāryanarasiṃhena pratyakṣādvaitam ucyate /
anumānapramāṇatvaṃ viśvasmin kaiś cid ucyate // [AgMsv_1.764]

plain_english: The all-knowing Lord, whose nature is nonconceptual and even perceptual, does not enter into ordinary practical usage.
sanskrit_cite:
tathā hi devaḥ sarvajño nirvikalpasvabhāvakaḥ /
sa cādhyakṣasvabhāvo 'pi nāyāti vyavahāryatām // [AgMsv_1.765]

plain_english: How could practical activity, which is conceptual by nature, arise in the nonconceptual? In fact, all ordinary practical activity is carried on through conceptualization.
sanskrit_cite:
avikalpe vikalpātmā vyavahāraḥ kathaṃ kila /
vikalpena ca sarvo 'yaṃ vyavahāro 'vatanyate // [AgMsv_1.766]

plain_english: That very process would be inference, consisting of conceptual constructions such as the subject, its property, pervasion, and the apprehension of these, and so on.
sanskrit_cite:
sa eva cānumānaṃ syāt tasyaitāḥ parikalpanāḥ /
pakṣataddharmatadvyāptitatpratītyādayo 'khilāḥ // [AgMsv_1.767]

plain_english: But in reality there is only one ultimate cognition. Yet one may object: how could inference exist in the absence of perception, since it depends on it?
sanskrit_cite:
vastutas tv eka evāsau pratyayaḥ pāramārthikaḥ /
nanv adhyakṣaviyoge syād anumānaṃ kathaṃ yataḥ // [AgMsv_1.768]

plain_english: It is true that inference depends on a connection determined by perception; but ultimately that rests on the one Lord who is the abode of omniscience.
sanskrit_cite:
tatpratyakṣaparicchinnapratibandhanibandhanam /
satyaṃ kiṃtu ya eko 'sau devaḥ sarvajñatāspadam // [AgMsv_1.769]

plain_english: Through immersion in that Lord, pervasion becomes possible in awareness; otherwise, even relations like fire and smoke, or knowledge of their absence, could not be established.
sanskrit_cite:
tadāveśavaśād eṣā vyāptir bodhe 'vakalpate /
anyathā vahnidhūmādi tadabhāvādivedanam // [AgMsv_1.770]

plain_english: The pattern of agreement and difference would not arise even over hundreds of ages; it arises because of similarity recognized by a primary cognition.
sanskrit_cite:
anvayavyatirekātmā na syād yugaśatair api /
ata eva hi mukhyasya mānasya sadṛśatvataḥ // [AgMsv_1.771]

plain_english: Inference is said to set practical activity in motion; thus all knowing subjects everywhere depend on the awareness of the Lord.
sanskrit_cite:
anumānam iti proktaṃ vyavahārapravartanam /
tad evam ete mātāraḥ sarvatreśvarasaṃvidam // [AgMsv_1.772]

plain_english: They come to be knowers by depending on that awareness, and not otherwise; for how could this ignorant class of beings become knowers without entering into it?
sanskrit_cite:
upajīvitum āyānti mātṛbhāvaṃ na cānyathā /
ajño hi jantuvargo 'yaṃ kathaṃ tadaniveśataḥ // [AgMsv_1.773]

plain_english: One attains the nature of a knower through that awareness; without it, how could knowerhood arise? Therefore this being's connection with awareness is not hard to obtain.
sanskrit_cite:
jñasvarūpatvam āpnoti tad vinā mātṛtā kutaḥ /
tasmād saṃvidi yogo 'sya sa ca nānena durlabhaḥ // [AgMsv_1.774]

plain_english: In reality there is no one apart from awareness, for each knower has awareness as its lord; thus any position operates only as drawn from the Lord's perception.
sanskrit_cite:
vastuto hi na kaś cit sa savinnātho hy asau tathā /
tad evaṃ pakṣam īśānapratyakṣākṣiptavṛttikam // [AgMsv_1.775]

plain_english: The bound means of knowing is said to be dependent on another; for this ignorant, non-sovereign being does not control its own pleasure and pain.
sanskrit_cite:
sāpekṣaṃ paratantre ca pāśavaṃ mānam ucyate /
ajño jantur anīśo 'yam ātmanaḥ sukhaduḥkhayoḥ // [AgMsv_1.776]

plain_english: The sage declared that the being moves only as impelled by the Lord; thus, for such a being, inference dependent on the Lord is the sole means of valid knowledge.
sanskrit_cite:
īśvaraprerito yātīty ata eva munir jagau /
evam īśvarasāpekṣānumānaikapramāṇatā // [AgMsv_1.777]

plain_english: This position was determined by the teacher named Lolaṭa and accepted by many; another thinker took it up and said, 'True, perceptual awareness also has validity.'
sanskrit_cite:
nirṇītā lolaṭākhyena guruṇā lokasaṃmatā /
anyas tadgṛhya evāha satyaṃ vādhyakṣasaṃvidaḥ // [AgMsv_1.778]

plain_english: In practical life, perception has validity; but how can inference be certain knowledge when error is so easily possible in it?
sanskrit_cite:
vyavahāre 'sti mānatvam anumā tu kathaṃ pramā /
sulabhavyabhicārāyām anumāyāṃ viniścitaḥ // [AgMsv_1.779]

plain_english: Who, standing as a careful examiner, could rest confidently on agreement and difference, which depend on presence in similar and dissimilar cases?
sanskrit_cite:
viśaṃśramītu ko nāma parīkṣakatayā sthitaḥ /
anvayo vyatirekaś ca yaḥ sapakṣetarasthitiḥ // [AgMsv_1.780]

plain_english: What is seen at first does not produce certainty at that moment; therefore it should be rejected because of faults such as defects in the subject and its property.
sanskrit_cite:
ādidṛṣṭas tadātve no viniścayavidhāyinau /
yais tu tasmād apāsyeta pakṣadharmādidūṣaṇāt [ṇam] // [AgMsv_1.781]

plain_english: They would be trying to purify a heap of filth with piles of dust; therefore inference remains as doubt, serving only as an aid to action.
sanskrit_cite:
varcaskakūṭe śuddhiṃ te kuryuḥ pāṃsukaṇoccayaiḥ /
tasmāt saṃśaya evāyaṃ pravṛttyaṅgatayā sthitaḥ // [AgMsv_1.782]

plain_english: Because it manifests difference, that same doubtful cognition is called māyā; and for bound beings, the means of knowing is māyā itself, arising from māyā and consciousness.
sanskrit_cite:
sa eva bhedābhāsitvān māyeti paribhāṣyate /
māyeva ca paśūnāṃ syān mānaṃ māyācidātakam // [AgMsv_1.783]

plain_english: Reasoning, which considers the possibility that one side may hold, serves to guide engagement or withdrawal in action by weighing the greater force of benefit or harm.
sanskrit_cite:
tarko vāpy ekapakṣāṃśasthitisaṃbhāvanātmakaḥ /
arthānarthabalīyastvāt pravṛttau [ttyai] vā nivṛttaye // [AgMsv_1.784]

plain_english: He alone is all-powerful; what need is there of other displays of means of knowledge? Śiva alone is the one knower, whose own limb this world appears as such.
sanskrit_cite:
prabhaviṣṇuḥ sa eveti kim anyair mānaḍambaraiḥ /
pramātā śiva evaiko yasyedaṃ svāṅgam īdrśam // [AgMsv_1.785]

plain_english: As an object, it appears on all sides as having the nature of certainty; but every other being, the bound soul, dwells in the midst of the darkness of doubt.
sanskrit_cite:
meyatvena samābhāti sarvato niścayātmakam /
anyaḥ punaḥ paśuḥ sarvaḥ saṃśayadhvāntamadhyagaḥ // [AgMsv_1.786]

plain_english: Colored by an awareness like a flash of lightning, he reaches a certainty that one of two alternatives is true and the other not.
sanskrit_cite:
saudāmanīdyutiprāyasaṃvitsamanurañjitaḥ /
pakṣadvitayasatyānyabhāvānyatamaniścayam // [AgMsv_1.787]

plain_english: Even while finding it, he never gains firm grounding here in any way; therefore it is established that all practical activity proceeds from reasoning.
sanskrit_cite:
vindāna eva labhate nātra rūḍhiṃ kathaṃ cana /
tad evaṃ tarkataḥ sarvo vyavahāra iti sthitam // [AgMsv_1.788]

plain_english: Let this very knowledge be designated as an impure means of knowledge; its impurity is just this, that it does not conform to the real object.
sanskrit_cite:
aśuddha saiva vidyeyam iti mānaṃ vidhīyatām /
aśuddhir iyatī tasyā yad vastv ananusāritā // [AgMsv_1.789]

plain_english: But others, being certain that there is no activity for one who has no purpose, argued in this way that needfulness alone is the assisting factor.
sanskrit_cite:
anye tv anarthino nāsti pravṛttir iti niścitāḥ /
arthitvam eva sacivam ity evaṃ paryacūcudan // [AgMsv_1.790]

plain_english: Thus those who know the self as other declared that desire has the status of a means of knowledge; but others say that even doubt does not arise about an elephant that is not determined at all.
sanskrit_cite:
rāgasya mānatām itthaṃ prāhur anyātmavedinaḥ /
anye tv āhuḥ saṃśayo 'pi na nāmāniścite gaje // [AgMsv_1.791]

plain_english: When there is capability, desire may arise for activity; therefore people, having slightly noticed their own agency, always engage in action.
sanskrit_cite:
śaktatve sati jāyeta rāgo vāpi pravṛttaye /
tataḥ svāṃ kartṛtām īṣad ālocya janatāḥ sadā // [AgMsv_1.792]

plain_english: Thus they engage in action; this would be merely the unfolding of limited agency. Therefore, whether that object is so or not, by that power he takes himself to be an agent.
sanskrit_cite:
pravartanta itītthaṃ syāt kalāyā eva jṛmbhitam /
tenārthaḥ sa tathā vāstu mā vābhūt svātmanas tayā // [AgMsv_1.793]

plain_english: Considering himself an agent, this person engages in action everywhere; but others say that the practical activity consisting of action is beginningless.
sanskrit_cite:
manvānaḥ kartṛtām eṣa sarvatraiva pravartate /
anye tv āhur anādir yo vyavahāraḥ kriyātmakaḥ // [AgMsv_1.794]

plain_english: That very restriction abides as the impeller of the whole world; and that same thing is called scripture, namely the traditional course of conduct of the elders.
sanskrit_cite:
niyatiḥ saiva viśvasya pravartakatayā sthitā /
sa eva cāgamo nāma vṛddhavyavahṛtikramaḥ // [AgMsv_1.795]

plain_english: Therefore this complete determination of dharma and so forth does not come from perception or inference, which are for the most part deceptive.
sanskrit_cite:
tataḥ samagra evāyaṃ dharmādipariniścayaḥ /
na pratyakṣān nānumānād bhūyasā vipralambhakam // [AgMsv_1.796]

plain_english: The mind of those inclined to examination comes to trust: children learn from others that food allays hunger and water allays thirst.
sanskrit_cite:
matir abhyeti viśvāsaṃ parīkṣāpakṣaśālinām /
annaṃ kṣudhaṃ śamayate tṛṣaṃ vārīti bālakāḥ // [AgMsv_1.797]

plain_english: Having ascertained it from elsewhere and not doubting that it is so, they also rely on that very source as the primary measure in other matters known by perception and so on.
sanskrit_cite:
anyataḥ pariniścitya tathātvānatiśaṅkinaḥ /
anyadākṣādike 'py arthe tata evādyamānataḥ // [AgMsv_1.798]

plain_english: Even examiners properly obtain certainty from what is declared by scripture; and so the sage said, regarding the pair, 'this is merit, this is demerit.'
sanskrit_cite:
labhante niścayaṃ samyag āgamākhyāt parīkṣakāḥ /
tathā ca munir āhedaṃ puṇyaṃ pāpam iti dvaye // [AgMsv_1.799]

plain_english: The purpose of a teaching text is small; that is not the purpose of scripture. For scripture is not merely a collection of books and written texts.
sanskrit_cite:
śāstraprayojanaṃ svalpaṃ nāgamasya prayojanam /
āgamo hi na nāmaiṣa pustakagranthasaṃcayaḥ // [AgMsv_1.800]

plain_english: It is not merely the well-known, beginningless Veda and the like; rather, scripture is that established tradition itself, and that tradition has the nature of speech.
sanskrit_cite:
kevalaṃ prathitābhikhyo 'nādir vedādikaḥ kila /
kiṃ tu prasiddhir evāsau sā ca śabdasvarūpiṇī // [AgMsv_1.801]

plain_english: That tradition, which in all systems never comes to be rejected, includes words for goats, shrines, matted hair, ashes, alms, staff, and water-pot.
sanskrit_cite:
yā sarvadarśaneṣv eva na jātv āyāty apohyatām /
chāgaiś caityo jaṭā bhasma bhikṣā daṇḍaḥ kamaṇḍaluḥ // [AgMsv_1.802]

plain_english: Net, heated stone, plucking of beard, hair, and body hair, fire, fuel, the piling of heaps of bricks, and the householder life.
sanskrit_cite:
jālaṃ taptaśilā śmaśrukeśalomaviluñcanam /
agnir edhā iṣṭakaughacayanaṃ gṛhamedhitā // [AgMsv_1.803]

plain_english: Apart from the course of established usage, what means is there for understanding, in terms of meaning, all such words and the assumed meanings of others?
sanskrit_cite:
ityādisarvaśabdānāṃ prasiddhiprakramād ṛte /
ko 'bhyupāyo 'rthataḥ kḷptatadanyārthāvabodhayoḥ // [AgMsv_1.804]

plain_english: Thus the wise have said that this scripture is a valid means of knowledge; for that established tradition is truly divine speech, since it does not deviate.
sanskrit_cite:
ittham āgama evāyaṃ pramāṇam iti dhīdhanaiḥ /
uktaṃ satyaiva vāg aiśī prasiddhir avigānataḥ // [AgMsv_1.805]

plain_english: Whether the well-known scripture in the world is reasonable or otherwise, it is an authority in both knowledge and ignorance; thus that is established.
sanskrit_cite:
prasiddha āgamo loke yuktimān athavetaraḥ /
vidyāyām apy avidyāyāṃ pramāṇam iti tat sthitam // [AgMsv_1.806]

plain_english: For the residents of the revered Bhūtaja, authoritativeness belongs to restriction; but others say that this distinct principle operating here is called time.
sanskrit_cite:
prāmāṇyaṃ niyateḥ śrīmadbhūtajāntanivāsinām /
anye tv āhur viśeṣo 'yaṃ kālo nāmābhivartate // [AgMsv_1.807]

plain_english: That present time operates with the nature of clear manifestation; but then it has an aspect whose clear nature belonged to the past and is now marked by non-clarity.
sanskrit_cite:
sphuṭabhāvasvabhāvo 'sau vartamāno 'bhivartate /
vṛttasphuṭasvabhāvāṃśas tadā tv asphuṭatāmayaḥ // [AgMsv_1.808]

plain_english: The past is conceived through the assumption of a cause, while the future is conceived as what is to come; but neither of these is in any way independent, because they depend on each other.
sanskrit_cite:
bhūtaḥ kāraṇakḷptyā tu bhāvy asau parikalpyate /
sa cāyaṃ na svatantro 'sti kaś cid anyonyasaṃśrayāt // [AgMsv_1.809]

plain_english: Time cannot stand independently because it leads to infinite regress, because forms are seen to reverse, because it has no fixed measure, and because it depends on both the knower and the known.
sanskrit_cite:
anavasthānato rūpaparāvṛttyavalokanāt /
iyattārūḍhyabhāvāc ca mātṛmeyobhayāśrayāt // [AgMsv_1.810]

plain_english: Time has no coherent nature of its own, because it never appears without conditions and because it cannot be consistently established as one or many, permanent or impermanent.
sanskrit_cite:
nirupādhikatadrūpapratibhānaviyogataḥ /
ekānekadhruvānityasvarūpānupapattitaḥ // [AgMsv_1.811]

plain_english: If a single thing has a single limiting condition, its unity does not require time; and if difference belongs to action or to the condition itself, that is explained internally, so time serves no purpose.
sanskrit_cite:
ekasyaikopadher aikyāt tirodher (?) upadherapi /
kriyāyāḥ svagate bhede kālasyānupayogataḥ // [AgMsv_1.812]

plain_english: Whether difference is produced by time itself or by something else through mutual dependence, the result is infinite regress; and since such conditioned difference is unreal and unsubstantial, it cannot establish time as truly real.
sanskrit_cite:
tatkṛte 'nyonyasaṃśrityānyakṛte 'py anavasthiteḥ /
aupādhikabhidāvṛtter asatyatvād avāstavāt // [AgMsv_1.813]

plain_english: Because time cannot be established as an effect and a single undivided thing does not need it, the clear sense of the present and its enduring presence are given by consciousness itself.
sanskrit_cite:
kāryasyānupapattitvād ekasyānupayogataḥ /
citaś ca sphuṭatādattavartamānasadātvataḥ // [AgMsv_1.814]
